rows.cihl: CIHL R1; CIHL R6; CIHL R89
rows.why: Civilians were reported killed. This engages the principle of distinction (ICRC Customary IHL Study, Rule 1) and the prohibition of murder (Rule 89; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Arts 27 and 32, and Additional Protocol I, Art. 51|niac: Common Article 3(1)(a) and Additional Protocol II, Arts 4 and 13]). Rule 6 is listed because it is the test to apply if a party says the victims were taking a direct part in hostilities. Under human rights law it engages the right to life (ICCPR, Art. 6).

rows.cihl: CIHL R1; CIHL R7; CIHL R11; CIHL R12; CIHL R14; CIHL R15
rows.iac: AP I 48; AP I 51(4)-(5); AP I 52; AP I 57
rows.why: The harm came from an attack, so the conduct-of-hostilities rules apply: distinction between civilians and military objectives (Rules 1 and 7), the ban on indiscriminate attacks (Rules 11-12), proportionality (Rule 14) and precautions in attack (Rule 15), set out in [iac: Additional Protocol I, Arts 48-57|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 13, with the detailed rules applying as customary law].

rows.cihl: CIHL R25; CIHL R28; CIHL R29; CIHL R31; CIHL R32; CIHL R55
rows.why: A medical facility, medical or aid worker, or relief operation was reportedly hit. These have specific protection (Rules 25 and 28-32; Rule 55 on relief) under [iac: Geneva Conventions I, II and IV and Additional Protocol I|niac: Common Article 3(2) and Additional Protocol II, Arts 9-11 and 18], and attacking them can be a war crime (Rome Statute, Art. 8(2)(b)(ix) and (xxiv), Art. 8(2)(e)(ii)-(iv)).

rows.cihl: CIHL R1; CIHL R89; CIHL R156
rows.why: The report describes a massacre or mass killing. Beyond murder (Rule 89), the facts are checked against crimes against humanity (Rome Statute, Art. 7) and, only if there is evidence of intent to destroy a protected group, genocide (Genocide Convention, Arts II-III; Rome Statute, Art. 6).

rows.iac: GC IV 27(2); AP I 75(2)(b); AP I 76; GC III 14
rows.why: Sexual or gender-based violence was reported. It is prohibited in all armed conflicts (Rule 93; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Art. 27(2); Additional Protocol I, Arts 75-76|niac: Common Article 3(1)(c); Additional Protocol II, Art. 4(2)(e)]) and rape and other sexual violence can be war crimes and crimes against humanity (Rome Statute, Arts 7(1)(g), 8(2)(b)(xxii), 8(2)(e)(vi)).

rows.iac: GC III 17, 87; GC IV 32; AP I 75(2)(a)(ii); GC I 12, 50; GC II 12, 51; GC III 130; GC IV 147
rows.why: Torture or cruel treatment of people in a party's power was reported. It is absolutely prohibited (Rule 90; [iac: Geneva Conventions III and IV, where torture is a grave breach|niac: Common Article 3(1)(a); Additional Protocol II, Art. 4(2)(a)]) and under human rights law (ICCPR, Art. 7; Convention against Torture).

rows.iac: GC III 99-108; GC IV 68, 75; GC III 130; GC IV 147
rows.why: A killing after capture or by sentence was reported. Executing people without a fair trial by a regularly constituted court is prohibited (Rules 89 and 100; [iac: Geneva Conventions III and IV|niac: Common Article 3(1)(d); Additional Protocol II, Art. 6]), and human rights law protects the right to life and to a fair trial (ICCPR, Arts 6 and 14).

People were reportedly abducted or held. Hostage-taking is prohibited (Rule 96; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Arts 34 and 147|niac: Common Article 3(1)(b); Additional Protocol II, Art. 4(2)(c)]) and arbitrary deprivation of liberty is unlawful (Rule 99; ICCPR, Art. 9).

rows.cihl: CIHL R53; CIHL R54; CIHL R55
rows.iac: AP I 54; AP I 70; GC IV 23, 55, 59
rows.why: Starvation, siege or blocked relief was reported. Starving civilians as a method of warfare and attacking objects they need to survive are prohibited (Rules 53-54; [iac: Additional Protocol I, Art. 54|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 14]), and parties must let relief through (Rule 55; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Arts 23 and 59|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 18]).

A journalist was reportedly harmed. Journalists are civilians and keep that protection (Rule 34; [iac: Additional Protocol I, Art. 79|niac: Common Article 3 and Additional Protocol II, Art. 13]); human rights law adds freedom of expression (ICCPR, Art. 19).

rows.cihl: CIHL R98; CIHL R99; CIHL R117; CIHL R123
rows.americas: ACHR 7; Inter-American Convention on Forced Disappearance
rows.why: Detention without due process or an enforced disappearance was reported (Rules 98-99, 117 and 123), engaging the right to liberty (ICCPR, Art. 9) and the Convention on Enforced Disappearance[iac: ; unlawful confinement of protected civilians is a grave breach (Geneva Convention IV, Art. 147)|niac: ; Common Article 3 and Additional Protocol II, Arts 4-5 set minimum guarantees for detainees].

rows.cihl: CIHL R129; CIHL R131; CIHL R132
rows.ihrl: ICCPR 12; Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement; Refugee Convention 33
rows.why: Forced displacement was reported. Civilians may not be displaced unless their security or imperative military reasons demand it (Rule 129; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Art. 49|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 17]), and displaced people have rights to shelter and return (Rules 131-132).

rows.cihl: CIHL R7; CIHL R50; CIHL R51; CIHL R52
rows.iac: Hague Regs 23(g), 28, 46-47; GC IV 33, 53; GC IV 147
rows.why: Civilian property was reportedly destroyed or looted. Destruction not required by military necessity and pillage are prohibited (Rules 50-52; [iac: Hague Regulations, Arts 23(g), 28, 46-47; Geneva Convention IV, Arts 33, 53 and 147|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 4(2)(g)]).

Repression or discrimination against a group was reported. This engages non-discrimination (Rule 88; ICCPR, Arts 2 and 26) and, where widespread or systematic, the crime against humanity of persecution (Rome Statute, Art. 7(1)(h)).

rows.iac: GC IV 24; AP I 77-78; GC IV 50
rows.why: Children are reported among those affected, so their special protection is added (Rule 135; [iac: Geneva Convention IV, Arts 24 and 50; Additional Protocol I, Arts 77-78|niac: Additional Protocol II, Art. 4(3)]; Convention on the Rights of the Child).

meta.label: Basis
meta.value: Indicative lookup prepared by Claude for Sara, 13 Nov 2026: provisions commonly engaged by each violation type (ICRC Customary IHL Study rules; Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols by conflict type; ICCPR, ICESCR, CAT, CEDAW, CRC, ICPPED; Rome Statute) and each location's armed-conflict context and regional system. Not a legal assessment: classification, parties, ratifications and reservations must be checked for each case.
